# Geopolitical Escalations and Latin American Equities

Report 134 | Published 2024-04-14 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2024-4-14/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/134.json)

Yield-curve normalization and Latin American exposure.

The explicit curve and bitcoin calls resolved favorably within their 18-month windows. Halving timing was protocol-driven and should carry little discretionary forecasting credit. Colombia remains a genuine future-horizon case; macro causal attribution and regional relative returns are not yet established.

**Coverage:** Read all macro, geopolitical, bitcoin, Latin American and gold sections. Explicit 18-month forecasts separated from conditional sector rotations and five-year Colombia thesis.

**Timing:** Eighteen months, to October 2025

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify the proposed causal mechanism.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

- [T10Y2Y observations](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/T10Y2Y) | FRED / originating statistical agency | 2026-11-07 | Verified in the audit

10 y minus 2 y spread moved from -0.38 points on April 12 2024 to +0.55 on October 14 2025. Companion T 10 Y 3 M moved from -0.95 to +0.01. Latest vintage downloaded and capped November 7; not a real-time backtest vintage.

- [September 2024 FOMC statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20240918a.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2024-09-18 | Verified in the audit

The Fed cut its target by 50 basis points to 4.75-5.00%, while describing inflation as still elevated and continuing securities runoff.

### 134-C23

**Reserve sanctions stimulate official gold demand.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | gold-reserve-demand |
| Source blocks | 140, 143 |
| Thesis family | gold-reserve-demand |

Official buying was large and survey respondents cited crisis risks, consistent with reserve-diversification concerns. The survey does not isolate sanctions from inflation, strategic targets or domestic production, so the singular sanctions mechanism is not established.

**Direction:** Separable components differ.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Evaluate the explanation separately from subsequent price direction.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [2024 central-bank gold survey](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/data/2024-central-bank-gold-reserves-survey) | World Gold Council | 2024-06-18 | Verified in the audit

Central banks added 1,037 tonnes in 2023 after 1,082 tonnes in 2022. Survey of 70 respondents conducted February-April 2024: 29% planned higher own gold reserves. Motives included strategic rebalancing, domestic production, crisis and inflation risk; survey intentions are not completed purchases.
